title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: share files from iPhone and iPad apps to start a Copilot Chat
summary: Hold: the briefing understates documented mobile data protection and account controls. Microsoft lists Copilot for iOS as supporting Intune app protection, while the briefing says its applicability is unconfirmed; blocking organisational Copilot Chat also does not establish that the iOS share target disappears.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not describe which signed-in account receives a file from this specific iOS sharing route.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Copilot app iOS iPhone iPad share Word Excel PowerPoint Files 500633 setting default account. Opened app overview, Manage Copilot Chat and Intune data-transfer guidance. They describe account separation or generic work identity, not this route's destination-account selection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Intune iOS app protection policies have a Receive data from other apps setting.
claims.quote: To specify how you want to allow an app to receive data from other apps, enable Receive data from other apps and then choose your preferred level of receiving data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; rationale: risk; Open questions
claims.claim: Intune app protection and Receive data from other apps are not confirmed to govern the Microsoft Copilot app.
claims.quote: These apps support the core App Protection Policy settings ... Restricting data transfer and copy-and-paste functions. Microsoft Copilot | iOS | [Core App Protection Policy settings] ✔
claims.fix: Replace the unconfirmed-applicability statements with: 'Microsoft lists Microsoft Copilot for iOS as supporting core Intune app protection policies, including data-transfer restrictions. Test how the assigned policy handles this share route.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/app-management/ref-protected-apps and https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/app-management/protection/manage-data-transfer-ios. Narrow the open question to how the assigned policy behaves on this particular sharing route, rather than whether the app supports protection.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app is the documented blocking path.
claims.quote: Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps. Select the Available Apps list. Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane. Select Block app.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The cited Integrated Apps documentation limits these controls to Global Admins.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: No API for blocking the Copilot app itself through Integrated Apps is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph block Copilot app Integrated Apps API copilot application availability; "Integrated Apps" "Copilot" "block" "Graph". Opened copilotPackage-unblock; read copilotPackage-block reference excerpt. These govern catalog packages, not the Copilot app itself.

claims.where: controls[1]; summary; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: No dedicated UI or API switch specific to the iOS share-to-chat feature is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "share" "iPhone" "chat" admin setting; "Copilot" "iOS" "share" "switch" "Graph". Opened configure-copilot-admin-center and Manage Copilot Chat; read sharing-settings excerpts. No dedicated inbound iOS sharing switch was found; response sharing is a different feature.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking Copilot in Integrated Apps removes the whole mobile app experience and therefore its iOS share target.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph block Copilot app Integrated Apps API copilot application availability. Opened Manage Copilot Chat, Integrated Apps guidance and app overview. These document blocking organisational Copilot access and a turned-off Chat screen, not removal of the iOS share target or personal app access.
claims.fix: Change controls[0].governs to 'Access to organisational Copilot Chat through the Copilot app'. Replace whole-app removal and share-target implications in its note and the prose with: 'Blocking Copilot through Integrated Apps blocks organisational Copilot Chat access, including for licensed users; blocked users see a Copilot Chat was turned off for your organization screen. Microsoft does not describe whether this removes the iOS share target.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/manage-copilot-chat. Do not present this as a control over personal Microsoft-account access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Blocking Copilot in Integrated Apps is the only documented tenant control relevant to this feature.
claims.quote: IT admins of work or school environments can limit their users from accessing the Copilot app with their Microsoft account (personal account) by using Tenant Restrictions.
claims.fix: Replace 'The only tenant control documented is blocking the Copilot app in Integrated Apps, which removes the whole app rather than this route' with 'Integrated Apps provides a control over organisational Copilot Chat access, rather than a dedicated switch for this sharing route.' Remove the implication that blocking the app is the only documented tenant control; retain the open question about a dedicated share-route switch without that exclusivity.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to check an Intune iOS app protection policy, but the controls table has no corresponding row.
claims.quote: Check whether your Intune app protection policy for iOS changes what the test does ... Intune's Receive data from other apps setting ... is not a row here.
claims.fix: Remove the standalone checklist item 'Check whether your Intune app protection policy for iOS changes what the test does, and record the result for your service desk.' Keep the managed-device sharing test and the corrected explanation of Intune's documented reach; this correction does not add a controls row.
